questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the labelled structures and choose the correct set of options accordingly.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement regarding the diagram given below.
options: Carboxylation is the most crucial step of the Calvin cycle where CO<sub>2</sub>is utilised for the carboxylation of RuBP.
The fixation of six molecules of CO<sub>2</sub>and 6 turns of the cycle are required for the formation of one molecule of glucose from the pathway.
For every CO<sub>2</sub>molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required.
The Calvin pathway may not occur in all photosynthetic plants; it does not matter whether they have C<sub>3</sub>or C<sub>4</sub>(or any other) pathways.
questions.solution: Let us at the outset understand very clearly that the Calvin pathway occurs in all photosynthetic plants; it does not matter whether they have C<sub>3</sub>or C<sub>4</sub>(or any other) pathways (Figure 11.8).  1. Carboxylation– Carboxylation is the fixation of CO<sub>2</sub>into a stable organic  intermediate. Carboxylation is the most crucial step of the Calvin cycle where CO<sub>2</sub>is utilised for the carboxylation of RuBP.  2. Reduction – These are a series of reactions that lead to the formation of glucose. The steps involve utilisation of 2 molecules of ATP for phosphorylation and two of NADPH for reduction per CO<sub>2</sub>molecule fixed. The fixation of six molecules of CO<sub>2</sub>and 6 turns of the cycle are required for the formation of one molecule of glucose from the pathway.  Hence for every CO<sub>2</sub>molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required. It is probably to meet this difference in the number of ATP and NADPH used in the dark reaction that the cyclic phosphorylation takes place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify and choose the correct labelled structures from the options given below for the diagram.

(i)-Mesophyll cell, (ii)-Plasmodesmata, (iii)-Mesophyll cell, (iv)-Atmospheric CO2, (v)-Reduction, (vi)-Transport, (vii)-Decarboxylation, (viii)-Fixation, (ix)-Regeneration, (x)-Cell wall, (xi)-Plasma membrane

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify and name the labelled structures respectively.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement regarding the diagram given below.
options: The primary CO<sub>2</sub>acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) and is present in the mesophyll cells.

The C4 acid OAA is formed in the mesophyll cells which then forms other 4-carbon compounds like malic acid or aspartic acid in the mesophyll cells itself, which are transported to the bundle sheath cells.
In the bundle sheath cells these C<sub>4</sub>acids are broken down to release CO<sub>2</sub>and a 3-carbon molecule and it is important to register that the bundle sheath cells lack RuBisCO enzyme.
The 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll where it  is converted to PEP again, thus, completing the cycle.
questions.solution: The primary CO<sub>2</sub>acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) and is present in the mesophyll cells. The enzyme responsible for this fixation is PEP carboxylase or PEPcase. It is important to register that the mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO enzyme. The C<sub>4</sub>acid OAA is formed in the mesophyll cells.  It then forms other 4-carbon compounds like malic acid or aspartic acid in the mesophyll cells itself, which are transported to the bundle sheath cells. In the bundle sheath cells these C<sub>4</sub>acids are broken down to release CO<sub>2</sub>and a 3-carbon molecule.  The 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll where it is converted to PEP again, thus, completing the cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Julius von Sachs provided evidence for production of glucose when plants grow
Reason: He found that the green parts in plants is where glucose is made, and that the glucose is usually stored as starch.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Julius von Sachs provided evidence for production of glucose when plants grow. Glucose is usually stored as starch. His later studies showed that the green substance in plants (chlorophyll as we know it now) is located in special bodies (later called chloroplasts) within plant cells. He found that the green parts in plants is where glucose is made, and that the glucose is usually stored as starch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In photosystem II electrons become excited
Reason: PS II has absorption maxima at 680 nm, and is called P680
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In photosystem II the reaction centre chlorophyll a absorbs 680 nm wavelength of red light causing electrons to become excited and jump into an orbit farther from the atomic nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Electrons are not used up in electron transport chain
Reason: In photosystem II the reaction centre chlorophyll a absorbs 680 nm wavelength of red light
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The electrons are not used up as they pass through the electron transport chain, but are passed on to the pigments of photosystem PS I.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Electrons in the reaction centre of PS I are transferred to another accepter molecule that has a greater redox potential
Reason: The reaction centre is different in both the photosystems
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Electrons in the reaction centre of PS I are also excited when they receive red light of wavelength 700 nm and are transferred to another accepter molecule that has a greater redox potential.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The whole scheme of transfer of electrons, starting from the PS II, uphill to the acceptor, down the electron transport chain to PS I is called Z scheme
Reason: Z scheme has been named due to the transport of protons in the process
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The whole electron transport process is called is called the Z scheme, due to its characterstic shape . This shape is formed when all the carriers are placed in a sequence on a redox potential scale.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Splitting of water is an essential step for PS II complex
Reason: The splitting of water is associated with PS I
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The electrons that were moved from photosystem II must be replaced. This is achieved by electrons available due to splitting of water. The splitting of water is associated with the PS II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Living organisms have the ability to carry energy and store it from oxidisable substances
Reason: Water splitting complex is associated with the PS II, which itself is physically located on the outer side of the membrane of the thylakoid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Living organisms have the capability of extracting energy from oxidisable substances and store this in the form of bond energy. Special substances like ATP, carry this energy in their chemical bonds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Photophosphorylation is important for energy production and storage
Reason: When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS I and then the PS II, a process called non-cyclic photo-phosphorylation occurs
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: ATP is synthesised by cells (in mitochondria and chloroplasts) is named phosphorylation. Photophosphorylation is the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: When only PS I is functional cyclic flow results in ATP synthesis
Reason: The two photosystems are connected through a thylakoid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: When only PS I is functional, the electron is circulated within the photosystem and the phosphorylation occurs due to cyclic flow of electrons. The excited electron does not pass on to NADP+ but is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain. The cyclic flow hence, results only in the synthesis of ATP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: ATP synthesis in photosynthesis is linked to development of a proton gradient across a membrane
Reason: Cyclic photophosphorylation does not occur when only light of wavelengths beyond 680 nm are available for excitation
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In photosynthesis , ATP synthesis is linked to development of a proton gradient across a membrane. These are the membranes of thylakoid. Here the proton accumulation is towards the inside of the membrane, i.e., in the lumen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The protons or hydrogen ions that are produced by the splitting of water accumulate within the lumen of the thylakoids
Reason: In respiration, protons accumulate in the intermembrane space of the ribosome
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Since splitting of the water molecule takes place on the inner side of the membrane, the protons or hydrogen ions that are produced by the splitting of water accumulate within the lumen of the thylakoids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: As electrons move through the photosystems, protons are transported across the membrane
Reason: ATP synthesis is linked to development of a neutron gradient across a membrane
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: As electrons move through the photosystems, protons are transported across the membrane. This happens because the primary accepter ofelectron which is located towards the outer side of the membrane transfers its electron not to an electron carrier but to an H carrier.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: A proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane as well as a measurable decrease in pH in the lumen is observed
Reason: The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the thylakoid side of the membrane
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Within the chloroplast, protons in the stroma decrease in number, while in the lumen there is accumulation of protons. This creates a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane as well as a measurable decrease in pH in the lumen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Proton gradient is important for ATP synthesis
Reason: Along with electrons that come from the acceptor of electrons of PS I, amino acids are necessary for the reduction of NADP+ to NADPH+ H+
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Proton gradient is important because it is the breakdown of this gradient that leads to the synthesis of ATP. The gradient is broken down due to the movement of protons across the membrane to the stroma.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: CF0 part of the ATP synthase enzyme protrudes on the outer surface of the thylakoid membrane on the side that faces the stroma
Reason: Energy is not used to pump protons across a membrane
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: CF0 is embedded in the thylakoid membrane and forms a transmembrane channel that carries out facilitated diffusion of protons across the membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: CF1 is embedded in the thylakoid membrane and forms a transmembrane channel
Reason: Chemiosmosis requires only ATP synthase
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: CF1 and protrudes on the outer surface of the thylakoid membrane on the side that faces the stroma. The break down of the gradient provides enough energy to cause a conformational change in the CF1 particle of the ATP synthase, which makes the enzyme synthesise several molecules of energypacked ATP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Biosynthetic phase produces amino acids
Reason: The process directly depends on the presence of light
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Processes leading to the synthesis of food, more accurately, sugars. is called the biosynthetic phase of photosynthesis. This process does not directly depend on the presence of light but is dependent on the products of the light reaction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: ATP synthase utilizes diffusion of electrons to produce ATP
Reason: ATP synthase has a channel that allows diffusion of electrons
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Energy is used to pump protons across a membrane, to create a gradient or a high concentration of protons within the thylakoid lumen. ATP synthase has a channel that allows diffusion of protons back across the membrane; this releases enough energy to activate ATP synthase enzyme that catalyses the formation of ATP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Biosynthetic phase of photosynthesis is not dependent on products of light reaction
Reason: When light becomes available the process stops
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Biosynthetic process does not directly depend on the presence of light but is dependent on the products of the light reaction, i.e., ATP and NADPH, besides CO2 and H2O. Immediately after light becomes unavailable, the biosynthetic process continues for some time, and then stops. If then, light is made available, the synthesis starts again.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: CO2 assimilation during photosynthesis is said to be of four main types
Reason: Oxaloacetic acid is identified as 5 carbon inorganic acid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: CO2 assimilation during photosynthesis was said to be of two main types: those plants in which the first product of CO2 fixation is a C3 acid (PGA), i.e., the C3 pathway, and those in which the first product was a C4 acid (OAA), i.e., the C4 pathway.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Acceptor molecule of dark reaction is a 2 carbon compound
Reason: those plants in which the first product of CO2 fixation is a C4 acid (PGA), i.e., the C4 pathway
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Acceptor molecule of dark reaction is a 5-carbon ketose sugar – ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Calvin cycle is described under four stages
Reason: Calvin and his co-workers then worked out the whole pathway and showed that the pathway operated in a non cyclic manner
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Calvin cycle can be described under three stages: carboxylation, reduction and regeneration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Carboxylation is the least crucial step of Calvin cycle
Reason: Calvin pathway does not occur in all photosynthetic plants
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Carboxylation is the most crucial step of the Calvin cycle where CO2 is utilised for the carboxylation of RuBP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The enzyme RuBP carboxylase has no other alternative name
Reason: The Calvin cycle proceeds in five stages
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Enzyme also has an oxygenation activity it would be more correct to call it RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase or RuBisCO.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Reduction reactions in Calvin cycle lead to the production of glucose
Reason: The fixation of six molecules of CO2 and 6 turns of the cycle are required for the formation of one molecule of glucose
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Reduction reactions in Calvin cycle lead to the production of glucose The steps involve utilisation of 2 molecules of ATP for phosphorylation and two of NADPH for reduction per CO2 molecule fixed. The fixation of six molecules of CO2 and 6 turns of the cycle are required for the formation of one molecule of glucose from the pathway.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Regeneration of the CO2 acceptor molecule RuBP is crucial for the Calvin cycle
Reason: It helps the cycle to continue in an uninterrupted manner
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Regeneration of the CO2 acceptor molecule RuBP is crucial if the cycle is to continue uninterrupted. The regeneration steps require one ATP for phosphorylation to form RuBP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Plants that are adapted to dry tropical regions have the C4 pathway
Reason: To make one molecule of glucose 6 turns of the cycle are required
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: C4 plants are special: They have a special type of leaf anatomy, they tolerate higher temperatures, they show a response to high light intensities, they lack a process called photorespiration and have greater productivity of biomass.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: C4 plants have Kranz anatomy in their leaves
Reason: For every CO2 molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The particularly large cells around the vascular bundles of the C4 plants are called bundle sheath cells, and the leaves which have such anatomy are said to have ‘Kranz’ anatomy. ‘Kranz’ means ‘wreath’ and is a reflection of the arrangement of cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Hatch and Slack pathway occurs in the mesophyll cells
Reason: Hatch and Slack pathway is a non cyclic process
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The primary CO2 acceptor in Hatch and Slack Pathway is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) and is present in the mesophyll cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. The basic pathway that results in the formation of the sugars, the Calvin pathway, is different in the C3 and C4 plants.
2. First step in Calvin cycle is CO2 fixation
3. RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for O2 when the CO2: O2 is nearly equal.
4. In photorespirationn, there is synthesis of sugars.
questions.solution: The first step of the Calvin pathway – the first CO2 fixation step. This is the reaction where RuBP combines with CO2 to form 2 molecules of 3PGA, that is catalysed by RuBisCO.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Rubisco is the most abundant enzyme in the world
2. Rubisco is named after its active sites
3. C3 plants show kranz anatomy.
4. Primary accceptor of hatch and slack pathway is present in bundle sheath cells.
questions.solution: RuBisCO that is the most abundant enzyme in the world is characterised by the fact that its active site can bind to both CO2 and O2– hence the name.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. In C3 plants, no O2 binds toRubisco
2. Rubisco has a much greater affinity for CO2
3. The C4 acid OAA is formed in the mesophyll cells.
4. In C3 plants some O2 does bind to RuBisCO, and hence CO2 fixation is increased.
questions.solution: RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for CO2 when the CO2: O2 is nearly equal. Imagine what would happen if this were not so! This binding is competitive. It is the relative concentration of O2 and CO2 that determines which of the two will bind to the enzyme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Photorespiration does not synthesize sugars
2. In photorespiration occuring in C3 plants RuBP is converted to C3 plants
3. There is a parabolic relationship between incident light and CO2 fixation rates at low light intensities.
4. The light saturation occurs at 10 per cent of the full sunlight.
questions.solution: In the photorespiratory pathway, there is neither synthesis of sugars, nor of ATP. Rather it results in the release of CO2 with the utilisation of ATP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Photorespiration does not occur in C4 plants
2. RuBisCO functions as a carboxylase minimising the oxygenase activity in C4 plants
3. The C3 and C4 plants respond same to CO2 concentrations.
4. The C4 plants show saturation at about 450 μlL-1
questions.solution: In C4 plants photorespiration does not occur. This is because they have a mechanism that increases the concentration of CO2 at the enzyme site.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. In PS I the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 800
2. In photosystem II the reaction centre chlorophyll a absorbs 680 nm wavelength
3. Each photosystem has all the pigments (except one molecule of chlorophyll a) forming a light harvesting system also called cytochrome
4. Accessory pigments facilitate photo-oxidation of chlorophyll a
questions.solution: In photosystem II the reaction centre chlorophyll a absorbs 680 nm wavelength of red light causing electrons to become excited and jump into an orbit farther from the atomic nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Internal CO2 concentration does not affect rate of photosynthesis
2. External plant factors do not affect rate of photosynthesis
3. some greenhouse crops such as tomatoes and bell pepper.
4. The dark reactions being enzymatic are temperature controlled.
questions.solution: Photosynthesis is under the influence of several factors, both internal (plant) and external. The plant factors include the number, size, age and orientation of leaves, mesophyll cells and chloroplasts, internal CO2 concentration and the amount of chlorophyll.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Most of the photosynthesis takes place in the green and yellow regions of the spectrum
2. Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment of photosynthesis
3. Accessory pigments cannot absorb light
4. Water stress causes the stomata to remain open hence increasing the CO2 availability.
questions.solution: The wavelengths at which there is maximum absorption by chlorophyll a, i.e., in the blue and the red regions, also shows higher rate of photosynthesis. Hence, we can conclude that chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. External factors affecting photosynthesis rate include mesophyll cells
2. Blackman's limiting factor comes into play when several factors affect any process
3. At any point the rate will be determined by the factor available at sub-optimal levels.
4. Including the plants in shade or in dense forests, light is rarely a limiting factor in nature.
questions.solution: When several factors affect any [bio] chemical process, Blackman’s (1905) Law of Limiting Factors comes into effect. This states the following: If a chemical process is affected by more than one factor, then its rate will be determined by the factor which is nearest to its minimal value: it is the factor which directly affects the process if its quantity is changed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Colour of leaves is due to four pigments
2. Chlorophyll a is yellow color in chromatogram
3. Xanthophyll is blue color in chromatogram
4. There is not a clear division of labour within the chloroplast.
5. Chlorophyll b is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis.
questions.solution: A chromatographic separation of the leaf pigments shows that the colour that we see in leaves is not due to a single pigment but due to four pigments: Chlorophyll a (bright or blue green in the chromatogram), chlorophyll b (yellow green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Incident light affects CO2 fixation rate
2. Usually one factor is not the major cause or is the one that limits the rate of photosynthesis
3. Most of the photosynthesis takes place in the blue and green regions of the spectrum.
4. These are named in the sequence in which they function during the light reaction., and not in the sequence of their discovery
questions.solution: While discussing light as a factor that affects photosynthesis, There is a linear relationship between incident light and CO2 fixation rates at low light intensities.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Water is the major limiting factor for photosynthesis
2. The concentration of CO2 is very high in the atmosphere (between 30 and 50 per cent)
3. The reaction centre is different in both the photosystems.
4. The concentration of CO2 is very low in the atmosphere (between 0.03 and 0.04 per cent)
questions.solution: Carbon dioxide is the major limiting factor for photosynthesis. The concentration of CO2 is very low in the atmosphere (between 0.03 and 0.04 per cent).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Reaction centre is different in both the photosystems
2. The LHC are made up of pigments which are not bound to proteins
3. PS II it has absorption maxima at 680 nm, and is called P680
4. The splitting of water is associated with the PS I
5. When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS II and then the PS I, a process called cyclic photo-phosphorylation occurs.
questions.solution: The reaction centre is different in both the photosystems. In PS I the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm, hence is called P700, while in PS II it has absorption maxima at 680 nm, and is called P680.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. The C3 and C4 plants respond differently to CO2 concentrations
2. C4 plants show saturation at about 360 µlL-1 while C3 responds to increased CO2 concentration and saturation is seen only beyond 450 µlL-1
3. The stroma lamellae membranes lack PS I as well as NADP reductase enzyme.
4. The cyclic flow results in the synthesis of ATP, and NADPH + H+.
questions.solution: The C3 and C4 plants respond differently to CO2 concentrations. At low light conditions neither group responds to high CO2 conditions. At high light intensities, both C3 and C4 plants show increase in the rates of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Synthesis of sugar is light reaction
2. Synthesis of ATP is dark reaction
3. Usually the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls of the mesophyll cells
4. Cyclic photophosphorylation also occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond 680 nm are available for excitation
questions.solution: Usually the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls of the mesophyll cells, such that they get the optimum quantity of the incident light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Dark reactions are solely water controlled
2. The C4 plants respond to lower temperatures
3. In chemiosmosis within the chloroplast, protons in the stroma decrease in number, while in the lumen there is accumulation of protons.
4. The ATP synthase enzyme consists of two parts: one called the CF0 and the other is CF1.
questions.solution: The dark reactions being enzymatic are temperature controlled. Though the light reactions are also temperature sensitive they are affected to a much lesser extent.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Tropical plants have higher temperature optimum
2. C3 plants have higher temperature optimum
3. Chemiosmosis requires a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient and ATP synthase
4. The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the lumen side of the membrane.
questions.solution: The temperature optimum for photosynthesis of different plants also depends on the habitat that they are adapted to. Tropical plants have a higher temperature optimum than the plants adapted to temperate climates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option:
1. Joseph Priestley provided evidence for production of glucose when plants grow
2. Julius von Sachs in 1770 performed a series of experiments that revealed the essential role of air in the growth of green plants
3. In green plants CO2 is the hydrogen donor and is oxidised to O2
4. T.W Engelmann (1730-1799) showed that sunlight is essential to the plant process that somehow purifies the air fouled by burning candles or breathing animals
questions.solution: Joseph Priestley (1733-1804) in 1770 performed a series of experiments that revealed the essential role of air in the growth of green plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Water is is not a reactant in light reaction
2. Water stress causes the stomata to open
3. Cornelius van Niel demonstrated that photosynthesis is essentially a light-dependent reaction in which hydrogen from a suitable oxidisable compound reduces carbon dioxide to carbohydrates.
4. CH2O represents a carbohydate
questions.solution: Water is one of the reactants in the light reaction, the effect of water as a factor is more through its effect on the plant, rather than directly on photosynthesis. Water stress causes the stomata to close hence reducing the CO2 availability.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. There are three photosystem
2. Water stress decreases the surface area of leaves
3. Photosynthesis is the secondary source of all food on earth
4. Jan ingenhousz discovered oxygen in 1774.
5. The O2 released is from water; this was proved using radio isobar techniques
questions.solution: Water stress makes leaves wilt, thus, reducing the surface area of the leaves and their metabolic activity as well.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ExperimentsFindings
A. Joseph Priestley's experiment with a candle and a mouse1) Air is restored by plants
B. Joseph Priestley's experiment with a mint plant2) Sunlight is necessary for releasing oxygen
C. Jan Ingenhousz's experiment with an aquatic plant in sunlight3) Candle extinguishes, mouse suffocates in closed jars
D. Jan Ingenhousz's experiment with aquatic plants in the dark4) Bubbles formed are oxygen
E. Plants in sunlight5) No bubbles formed, indicating lack of oxygen release
questions.solution:
A - 3: Joseph Priestley observed that in a closed bell jar, both the candle and mouse would suffocate or extinguish due to the depletion of oxygen, demonstrating that both combustion and respiration use up the air (oxygen).
B - 1: When Priestley placed a mint plant in the same bell jar, he found that the air was "restored," allowing the candle to burn again and the mouse to survive, showing that plants release a substance (oxygen) that restores the air.
C - 4: Ingenhousz's experiment with an aquatic plant showed that in bright sunlight, bubbles formed around the green parts of the plant. He identified these bubbles as oxygen, indicating that photosynthesis occurs in the presence of sunlight.
D - 5: In the absence of sunlight (dark conditions), Ingenhousz observed that no bubbles formed around the aquatic plant, indicating no oxygen release, and hence, no photosynthesis.
E - 2: Plants exposed to sunlight release oxygen, highlighting that sunlight is essential for the photosynthetic process that purifies the air.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ExperimentObservation
A. Joseph Priestley1) Plants restore air quality.
B. Jan Ingenhousz2) Sunlight is essential for purifying air.
C. Candle in a closed jar3) Air becomes "damaged."
D. Mouse in a closed jar4) Suffocates due to lack of air.
questions.solution:
A - 4: Joseph Priestley concluded that plants restore the air quality.
B - 2: Jan Ingenhousz demonstrated that sunlight is essential for plants to purify the air.
C - 3: A burning candle in a closed jar "damages" the air, causing it to extinguish.
D - 1: A mouse in a closed jar suffocates due to a lack of breathable air.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ScientistKey Findings
A. Photosynthesis Equation1. Identified glucose production in plants and its storage as starch.
B. T.W. Engelmann2. Used a prism to determine the action spectrum of photosynthesis.
C. Cornelius van Niel3. Demonstrated that photosynthesis involves light-dependent reactions and identified water as the hydrogen donor in green plants.
D. Julius von Sachs4. CO₂ + H₂O + Light → [CH₂O] + O₂
questions.solution:
A - 4: The overall equation for photosynthesis is CO₂ + H₂O + Light → [CH₂O] + O₂.
B - 2: T.W. Engelmann used a prism to identify the action spectrum of photosynthesis by detecting oxygen evolution.
C - 3: Cornelius van Niel showed that photosynthesis involves light-dependent reactions and that in green plants, water is the hydrogen donor.
D - 1: Julius von Sachs demonstrated that plants produce glucose which is stored as starch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Component of ChloroplastFunction
A. Grana1. Site of ATP and NADPH synthesis.
B. Stroma Lamellae2. Connects grana and facilitates the transport of molecules.
C. Stroma3. Site of enzymatic reactions that synthesize sugar from ATP and NADPH.
D. Light Reactions4. Light-driven reactions producing ATP and NADPH.
questions.solution:
A - 4: Grana are the sites where light reactions occur, involving the synthesis of ATP and NADPH.
B - 2: Stroma lamellae connect the grana and facilitate the transport of molecules between them.
C - 3: The stroma is where the dark reactions (carbon reactions) occur, using ATP and NADPH to synthesize sugars.
D - 1: Light reactions are driven by light and produce ATP and NADPH.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
PigmentColor
A. Chlorophyll a1. Blue-green color, absorbs light maximally at 430 nm and 662 nm.
B. Chlorophyll b2. Yellow-green color, assists in photosynthesis by capturing light.
C. Xanthophylls3. Yellow color, helps in light absorption and protection.
D. Carotenoids4. Yellow to yellow-orange color, aids in light absorption and protection.
questions.solution:
A - 4: Chlorophyll a is blue-green and absorbs light maximally at around 430 nm (blue) and 662 nm (red).
B - 2: Chlorophyll b is yellow-green and assists in capturing light for photosynthesis.
C - 3: Xanthophylls are yellow pigments that help in light absorption and provide protection.
D - 1: Carotenoids are yellow to yellow-orange and play roles in light absorption and protection.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ObservationRelated Finding
A. Maximum absorption of chlorophyll a1. Occurs in the blue and red regions of the spectrum.
B. Maximum photosynthesis rate2. Correlates with wavelengths of maximum chlorophyll a absorption.
C. Chlorophyll a as the chief pigment3. Blue (around 430 nm) and red (around 662 nm).
D. Wavelengths at which chlorophyll a shows absorption peaks4. Responsible for the majority of photosynthesis in plants.
questions.solution:
A - 1: Chlorophyll a shows maximum absorption in the blue and red regions.
B - 2: The highest rate of photosynthesis occurs at wavelengths where chlorophyll a absorbs maximally.
C - 4: Chlorophyll a is the primary pigment responsible for the majority of photosynthesis in plants.
D - 3: Chlorophyll a has absorption peaks in the blue (around 430 nm) and red (around 662 nm) regions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ComponentFunction
A. Photosystem I (PS I)1. Absorption peak at 680 nm, known as P680.
B. Photosystem II (PS II)2. Absorption peak at 700 nm, known as P700.
C. Light Harvesting Complex (LHC.3. Organizes pigments into complexes to absorb different wavelengths of light.
D. Reaction Centre4. Site where high-energy chemical intermediates are formed.
questions.solution:
A - 2: Photosystem I (PS I) has a reaction centre chlorophyll a with an absorption peak at 700 nm, known as P700.
B - 1: Photosystem II (PS II) has a reaction centre chlorophyll a with an absorption peak at 680 nm, known as P680.
C - 3: The Light Harvesting Complex (LHC) organizes pigments to absorb various wavelengths of light.
D - 4: The reaction centre is where high-energy chemical intermediates, ATP and NADPH, are formed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Photosynthetic ComponentsFunction
A. Excited Electrons in PS II1. Reduce NADP+ to NADPH + H+.
B. NADP+2. Passes electrons through a series of cytochromes.
C. Excited Electrons in PS I3. Absorbs light at 680 nm to excite electrons.
D. Electron Transport Chain4. Moves electrons downhill from PS II to PS I.
questions.solution:
A - 3: Excited electrons in PS II are absorbed at 680 nm and excited to a higher energy state.
B - 1: NADP+ is reduced to NADPH + H+ when it accepts electrons.
C - 4: Excited electrons in PS I are moved downhill to reduce NADP+.
D - 2: The electron transport chain passes electrons through cytochromes from PS II to PS I.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ProcessesDetails
A. Proton Gradient Formation1. Protons accumulate in the lumen due to water splitting and electron transport.
B. Water Splitting2. Reduces NADP+ to NADPH + H+ by removing protons from the stroma.
C. NADP Reductase Enzyme3. Creates protons and electrons, which accumulate in the thylakoid lumen.
D. Proton Accumulation in Lumen4. Leads to a decrease in pH and creation of a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane.
questions.solution:
A - 1: Proton gradient formation occurs as protons accumulate in the lumen due to water splitting and electron transport.
B - 3: Water splitting creates protons and electrons that accumulate in the thylakoid lumen.
C - 2: NADP reductase enzyme reduces NADP+ to NADPH + H+ by removing protons from the stroma.
D - 4: Proton accumulation in the lumen decreases pH and creates a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ComponentsFunctions
A. CF01. Embedded in the thylakoid membrane; facilitates proton diffusion.
B. CF12. Catalyzes the formation of ATP by utilizing the energy from the proton gradient.
C. ATP Synthase3. Composed of CF0 and CF1; synthesizes ATP using the energy from the proton gradient.
D. Proton Gradient4. Created by the movement of protons across the thylakoid membrane; drives ATP synthesis.
questions.solution:
A - 4: CF0 is embedded in the thylakoid membrane and facilitates proton diffusion.
B - 2: CF1 catalyzes the formation of ATP by utilizing the energy from the proton gradient.
C - 3: ATP synthase is composed of CF0 and CF1 and synthesizes ATP using the energy from the proton gradient.
D - 1: The proton gradient is created by the movement of protons across the thylakoid membrane and drives ATP synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ProcessesDetails
A. Calvin Cycle1. Produces ATP and NADPH, which are used in the biosynthetic phase.
B. Light Reaction2. Uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO2 into sugars.
C. Chemiosmosis3. Creates a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane to drive ATP synthesis.
D. Radioisotope 14C Experiment4. Used by Melvin Calvin to discover the first CO2 fixation product and the Calvin cycle.
questions.solution:
A - 2: The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO2 into sugars.
B - 1: The light reaction produces ATP and NADPH, which are used in the biosynthetic phase.
C - 3: Chemiosmosis creates a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane to drive ATP synthesis.
D - 4: The radioisotope 14C experiment was used by Melvin Calvin to discover the first CO2 fixation product and the Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Stages of Calvin CycleDetails
A. Regeneration1. Fixation of CO2 into a stable organic intermediate; catalyzed by RuBisCO.
B. Reduction2. Involves the use of ATP and NADPH to convert 3-PGA into glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P).
C. Carboxylation3. Regeneration of RuBP from G3P to enable the cycle to continue.
D. RuBisCO4. Enzyme that catalyzes the fixation of CO2 and also has oxygenation activity.
questions.solution:
A - .3: Regeneration involves the conversion of G3P back to RuBP to continue the cycle.
B - 2: Reduction involves the use of ATP and NADPH to convert 3-PGA into glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P).
C - 1: Carboxylation involves the fixation of CO2 into a stable organic intermediate, catalyzed by RuBisCO
D - 4: RuBisCO is the enzyme that catalyzes the fixation of CO2 and has oxygenation activity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Pathway ComponentsFunctions
A. RuBP1. The molecule that accepts CO2 to begin the Calvin cycle.
B. 3-PGA2. A stable organic intermediate produced from the carboxylation of RuBP.
C. Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P)3.Energy carriers used in the reduction phase of the Calvin cycle.
D. ATP and NADPH4. The product formed after the reduction of 3-PGA.
questions.solution:
A - 1: RuBP is the molecule that accepts CO2 at the start of the Calvin cycle.
B - 2: 3-PGA is the stable organic intermediate produced from the carboxylation of RuBP.
C - 4: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P) is the product formed after the reduction of 3-PGA.
D - 3: ATP and NADPH are energy carriers used in the reduction phase of the Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Components of Calvin CycleRequirements or Functions
A. CO21. Molecule that enters the Calvin cycle and requires energy for fixation.
B. ATP2. Required in the Calvin cycle; 3 molecules are needed per CO2 molecule fixed.
C. NADPH3. A process that produces additional ATP to balance the ATP and NADPH requirements.
D. Cyclic Phosphorylation4. Required in the Calvin cycle; 2 molecules are needed per CO2 molecule fixed.
questions.solution:
A - 1: CO2 is the molecule that enters the Calvin cycle and requires energy (ATP and NADPH) for fixation.
B - 2: ATP is required in the Calvin cycle, with 3 molecules needed for every CO2 molecule fixed.
C - 4: NADPH is also required in the Calvin cycle, with 2 molecules needed per CO2 molecule fixed.
D - 3: Cyclic phosphorylation produces additional ATP to balance the difference in the number of ATP and NADPH required in the Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Features of C4 PlantsCharacteristics
A. Kranz Anatomy1. Special leaf anatomy with bundle sheath cells arranged in a wreath-like pattern.
B. Tolerance to High Temperatures2. Adapted to withstand higher temperatures compared to C3 plants.
C. Response to High Light Intensities3. Efficient in utilizing high light levels for photosynthesis.
D. Lack of Photorespiration4. Avoids the process of photorespiration, leading to more efficient carbon fixation.
questions.solution:
A - 4: C4 plants lack photorespiration, which allows them to fix carbon more efficiently than C3 plants.
B - 2: C4 plants are adapted to tolerate higher temperatures compared to C3 plants.
C - 3: They show a strong response to high light intensities, enhancing their photosynthetic efficiency.
D- 1: Kranz Anatomy refers to the special leaf anatomy of C4 plants, where bundle sheath cells are arranged in a wreath-like pattern around the vascular bundles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Adaptations of C4 PlantsFunctions
A. Bundle Sheath Cells1. Have thick walls that are impervious to gaseous exchange and contain many chloroplasts.
B. Mesophyll Cells2. Found surrounding the bundle sheath cells and are involved in the initial fixation of CO2.
C. Efficient Carbon Fixation3. Results from the lack of photorespiration and the presence of specialized leaf anatomy.
D. Lack of Intercellular Spaces4. Helps in reducing the loss of CO2 and preventing photorespiration.
questions.solution:
A - 4: The lack of intercellular spaces in bundle sheath cells helps in reducing CO2 loss and preventing photorespiration.
B - 2: Mesophyll cells are responsible for the initial fixation of CO2 in C4 plants.
C - 3: C4 plants achieve efficient carbon fixation due to their lack of photorespiration and specialized leaf structure.
D- 1: Bundle sheath cells in C4 plants have thick walls and are rich in chloroplasts, forming a key part of the Kranz anatomy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
ComponentsFunctions or Locations
A. Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP)1. Primary CO2 acceptor in mesophyll cells.
B. Bundle Sheath Cells2. Enzyme responsible for fixing CO2 to PEP.
C. PEP Carboxylase (PEPcase)3. Site of Calvin cycle in C4 plants.
D. RuBisCO4. Enzyme that fixes CO2 in the Calvin cycle and is located in bundle sheath cells.
questions.solution:
A - 1: Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) is the primary CO2 acceptor located in the mesophyll cells.
B - 3: The Calvin cycle, which is common to all plants, occurs in the bundle sheath cells of C4 plants.
C - 2: PEP Carboxylase (PEPcase) is the enzyme responsible for fixing CO2 to PEP in the mesophyll cells.
D - 4: RuBisCO is the enzyme that fixes CO2 in the Calvin cycle and is located in the bundle sheath cells of C4 plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Factors Affecting PhotosynthesisCharacteristics or Effects
A. Internal Factors1. Includes sunlight, temperature, CO2 concentration, and water.
B. External Factors2. Includes the number, size, and age of leaves, mesophyll cells, and chloroplasts.
C. Blackman’s Law of Limiting Factors3. The rate of a process is determined by the factor that is nearest to its minimal value.
D. Rate of Photosynthesis4. Will be determined by the limiting factor when several factors are not at optimal levels.
questions.solution:
A - 2: Internal factors affecting photosynthesis include characteristics of the plant such as the number, size, and age of leaves, mesophyll cells, and chloroplasts.
B - 1: External factors affecting photosynthesis include sunlight, temperature, CO2 concentration, and water availability.
C - 3: Blackman’s Law of Limiting Factors states that the rate of a process is determined by the factor that is nearest to its minimal value.
D - 4: The rate of photosynthesis will be determined by the limiting factor when several factors are not at optimal levels.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Example of Limiting FactorsApplication
A. Light1. Can be a limiting factor if it is sub-optimal even if CO2 and temperature are optimal.
B. Temperature2. Can limit photosynthesis if it is too low despite adequate light and CO2.
C. CO2 Concentration3. Can be a limiting factor if it is low even if light and temperature conditions are ideal.
D. Water4. Essential for photosynthesis and can be a limiting factor if not available even under optimal light, CO2, and temperature conditions.
questions.solution:
A - 4: Light can be a limiting factor for photosynthesis if it is not at optimal levels, regardless of CO2 and temperature conditions.
B - 2: Temperature can limit photosynthesis if it is too low, even if light and CO2 levels are optimal.
C - 3: CO2 concentration can be a limiting factor if it is too low, even if light and temperature are optimal.
D - 1: Water is crucial for photosynthesis and can limit the process if it is not available, regardless of optimal light, CO2, and temperature conditions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Factors Influencing PhotosynthesisEffects or Characteristics
A. Carbon Dioxide (CO2)1. C4 plants show saturation at about 360 µL L⁻¹ CO2.
B. Temperature2. Dark reactions are temperature controlled, and the temperature optimum varies with the plant habitat.
C. Water3. Water stress causes stomatal closure and reduced CO2 availability, leading to wilting and decreased metabolic activity.
questions.solution:
A - 1: C4 plants show saturation of photosynthesis at around 360 µL L⁻¹ CO2, while C3 plants show saturation only beyond 450 µL L⁻¹.
B - 3: Water stress impacts photosynthesis indirectly by causing stomatal closure, reducing CO2 availability, and leading to wilting and decreased leaf surface area and metabolic activity.
C - 2: Temperature affects dark reactions significantly and the optimum temperature for photosynthesis varies depending on the plant’s habitat, with tropical plants having a higher optimum compared to temperate plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

Engelmann described the first action spectrum of photosynthesis in 1882 (d-i). Hence the correct match is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cyclic photophosphorylation occurs in the stroma lamellae of the chloroplast.
Reason (R): Stroma lamellae membrane lacks both PS II and the NADP reductase enzyme.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because cyclic photophosphorylation is known to occur in the stroma lamellae.

Reason (R) is correct and provides the correct explanation for the Assertion. The stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II as well as the NADP reductase enzyme. Due to the absence of these components, the excited electron from PS I cannot pass on to NADP$^{+}$. Instead, it is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain, forcing the cyclic flow of electrons which results only in the synthesis of ATP.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the Calvin cycle, the reduction step requires 2 ATP and 2 NADPH for every C$O_{2}$ molecule fixed. \\ Statement II: To synthesize one molecule of glucose, the C_{4}$ pathway requires 12 more ATP molecules than the C_{3}$ pathway.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: The Calvin cycle consists of three stages: carboxylation, reduction, and regeneration. The reduction step specifically utilizes 2 molecules of ATP for phosphorylation and 2 molecules of NADPH for reduction per CO_{2}$ molecule fixed. \\ \\ Statement II is correct: The synthesis of one glucose molecule requires the fixation of 6 CO_{2}$ molecules. In the C_{3}$ pathway, this requires 18 ATP (3 ATP per CO_{2}\times$ 6). In the C_{4}$ pathway, this requires 30 ATP (5 ATP per CO_{2}\times$ 6). The difference is 30 - 18 = 12 ATP molecules.

Thus, both statements are correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the Calvin cycle, the assimilatory power (ATP and NADPH) generated during the light reaction is consumed. Identify the correct statement regarding their utilization in the different stages of the cycle:
options: ATP is consumed during carboxylation and reduction, whereas NADPH is consumed only during reduction.
ATP is consumed during reduction and regeneration, whereas NADPH is consumed only during reduction.
Both ATP and NADPH are consumed during the reduction and regeneration stages.
ATP is consumed only during reduction, whereas NADPH is consumed during both reduction and regeneration.
questions.solution:
The Calvin cycle (biosynthetic phase) consists of three main stages: carboxylation, reduction, and regeneration.

1. Carboxylation is the fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ into a stable organic intermediate (3-PGA). This step does not consume ATP or NADPH.

2. Reduction involves a series of reactions that lead to the formation of glucose. This step utilizes both ATP (for phosphorylation) and NADPH (for reduction).

3. Regeneration is the crucial step of reforming the $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor molecule RuBP, which requires one molecule of ATP for phosphorylation but no NADPH.

Therefore, ATP is consumed in both the reduction and regeneration stages, whereas NADPH is consumed only in the reduction stage.

Answer: ATP is consumed during reduction and regeneration, whereas NADPH is consumed only during reduction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A $C_3$ plant is exposed to high temperature and high light intensity, leading to the closure of its stomata. Under these conditions, what will RuBisCO primarily bind to, and what are the immediate products formed in the reaction?
options: $\text{O}_2$; one molecule of phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate
questions.solution:
Under high temperature and high light intensity, the stomata of $C_3$ plants close to prevent water loss. This stops the entry of atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$, while $\text{O}_2$ continues to accumulate inside the leaf due to the ongoing photolysis of water in the light reactions.

Because the binding of $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ to the active site of RuBisCO is competitive, the high $\text{O}_2$ to $\text{CO}_2$ ratio forces the enzyme to function primarily as an oxygenase.

In this photorespiratory pathway, RuBisCO binds $\text{O}_2$ to RuBP (a 5-carbon compound), splitting it to form one molecule of a 3-carbon compound (phosphoglycerate) and one molecule of a 2-carbon compound (phosphoglycolate). It does not form two molecules of phosphoglycerate as it would during normal carboxylation.

Answer: $\text{O}_2$; one molecule of phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the stages of the Calvin cycle in List I with their corresponding energy requirements in List II.

List IList II
A. Carboxylation per $CO_2$ fixedI. $1$ ATP
B. Reduction per $CO_2$ fixedII. $18$ ATP and $12$ NADPH
C. Regeneration per $CO_2$ fixedIII. $0$ ATP and $0$ NADPH
D. Total requirement for $1$ GlucoseIV. $2$ ATP and $2$ NADPH

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In the Calvin cycle:

Carboxylation is the fixation of $CO_2$ into a stable organic intermediate and does not require ATP or NADPH.

Reduction involves the utilization of $2$ molecules of ATP for phosphorylation and $2$ molecules of NADPH for reduction per $CO_2$ molecule fixed.

Regeneration of the $CO_2$ acceptor molecule RuBP requires $1$ ATP for phosphorylation.

To synthesize one molecule of glucose, $6$ turns of the cycle are required, consuming a total of $18$ ATP and $12$ NADPH.

Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The ATP and NADPH synthesized during the light reaction of photosynthesis are immediately utilized in which of the following cellular locations?
questions.solution:
The light reaction of photosynthesis produces ATP, NADPH, and $\mathrm{O}_2$ in the thylakoids. While $\mathrm{O}_2$ diffuses out of the chloroplast as a waste product, ATP and NADPH do not leave the organelle. Instead, they are immediately consumed in the stroma of the chloroplast to drive the biosynthetic phase (dark reaction), which involves the reduction of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ into sugars.

They are not transported to the cytoplasm or mitochondrial matrix for general cellular use, and the thylakoid lumen is the site of proton accumulation rather than the site of ATP and NADPH utilization.

Answer: Stroma of the chloroplast

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In $C_3$ plants, some $\text{O}_2$ binds to RuBisCO, resulting in a decrease in $\text{CO}_2$ fixation.
Reason (R): RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for $\text{O}_2$ than for $\text{CO}_2$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: In $C_3$ plants, RuBisCO can bind to $\text{O}_2$ instead of $\text{CO}_2$ due to its dual catalytic nature. When $\text{O}_2$ binds to RuBisCO, the wasteful process of photorespiration is initiated, which utilizes ATP and releases $\text{CO}_2$ without synthesizing sugars, thereby decreasing the overall $\text{CO}_2$ fixation.

Reason (R) is false: According to NCERT, RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for $\text{CO}_2$ than for $\text{O}_2$. The binding of these gases is competitive, and it is the relative concentration of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ at the active site that determines which of the two will bind to the enzyme. The occurrence of photorespiration does not mean RuBisCO has a higher intrinsic affinity for $\text{O}_2$.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
A. Water splitting complexI. $\text{C}_4$ plants
B. Universal biosynthetic pathwayII. Photosystem II
C. Kranz anatomyIII. Chemiosmosis
D. ATP synthesis mechanismIV. Calvin cycle

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The water splitting complex is physically associated with Photosystem II (PS II) on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane (A-II).

The Calvin cycle is the universal biosynthetic pathway for the synthesis of sugars in all plants, whether they are $\text{C}_3$ or $\text{C}_4$ (B-IV).

Kranz anatomy is a characteristic feature of the leaves of $\text{C}_4$ plants, where bundle sheath cells form several layers around the vascular bundles (C-I).

ATP synthesis in chloroplasts is explained by the chemiosmotic hypothesis, which requires a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient, and ATP synthase (D-III).

Thus, the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Sugarcane, what is the first stable product of $\text{CO}_2$ fixation and in which specific cells is it formed?
options: Oxaloacetic acid in bundle sheath cells
questions.solution:
Sugarcane is a $\text{C}_4$ plant exhibiting Kranz anatomy. In $\text{C}_4$ plants, the initial $\text{CO}_2$ fixation occurs in the mesophyll cells where Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) acts as the primary acceptor in the presence of PEP carboxylase to form the 4-carbon compound Oxaloacetic acid (OAA).

Thus, OAA is the first stable product and it is formed in the mesophyll cells. The Calvin cycle (where PGA is formed) occurs later in the bundle sheath cells. Students often confuse the location of initial fixation or mistake Sugarcane for a $\text{C}_3$ plant.

Answer: Oxaloacetic acid in mesophyll cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the Hatch-Slack pathway, the $C_{4}$ acid formed in the mesophyll cells is transported to the bundle sheath cells. What is the immediate primary metabolic event that this $C_{4}$ acid undergoes upon entering the bundle sheath cells?
questions.solution:
In the $C_{4}$ pathway (Hatch-Slack pathway), the $C_{4}$ acid (such as malic acid or aspartic acid) formed in the mesophyll cells is transported to the bundle sheath cells.

Upon entering the bundle sheath cells, these $C_{4}$ acids undergo decarboxylation. They are broken down to release $CO_{2}$ and a 3-carbon molecule.

The released $CO_{2}$ then enters the Calvin cycle ($C_{3}$ pathway) catalyzed by RuBisCO, while the 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll to regenerate PEP.

Answer: Decarboxylation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding photosystems:
(A) In PS I, the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm.
(B) The reaction centre of PS II is called P680.
(C) Stroma lamellae possess both PS I and PS II.
(D) PS II is involved in cyclic photophosphorylation.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as the reaction centre of Photosystem I (PS I) is P700, having an absorption peak at 700 nm.

Statement (B) is correct as the reaction centre of Photosystem II (PS II) has an absorption maximum at 680 nm and is called P680.

Statement (C) is incorrect because stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II and NADP reductase enzyme; they possess only PS I.

Statement (D) is incorrect because PS II is involved only in non-cyclic photophosphorylation, whereas cyclic photophosphorylation involves only PS I.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the products of the light reaction:
(A) Oxygen is released into the thylakoid lumen and eventually diffuses out of the chloroplast.
(B) ATP is synthesized on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane and remains in the chloroplast.
(C) NADPH is transported into the cytoplasm to drive the synthesis of sugars.
(D) The biosynthetic phase depends directly on the products of the light reaction.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct because the water-splitting complex is located on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, releasing oxygen into the lumen, which then diffuses out of the chloroplast.

Statement (B) is correct as the $CF_1$ portion of ATP synthase protrudes towards the stroma, releasing ATP into the stroma where it is retained for the dark reaction.

Statement (C) is incorrect because NADPH is produced on the stroma side by NADP reductase and is utilized within the stroma itself for the Calvin cycle; it is not transported to the cytoplasm.

Statement (D) is correct because the biosynthetic phase (dark reaction) strictly depends on the assimilatory power (ATP and NADPH) produced during the light reaction.

Thus, three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During a specific light reaction process in chloroplasts, an excited electron is not transferred to $\text{NADP}^+$ but cycles back to the reaction centre complex via the electron transport chain. Which of the following statements is correct regarding this specific event?
options: It requires the splitting of water to supply continuous electrons.
It occurs in membrane regions that lack the NADP reductase enzyme.
It occurs primarily in grana lamellae where both photosystems are functional.
It results in the simultaneous synthesis of both ATP and $\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+$.
questions.solution:
The process described in the question is cyclic photophosphorylation, where the electron is circulated within Photosystem I (PS I).

This process occurs in the stroma lamellae, which lack both PS II and the NADP reductase enzyme. Because it lacks PS II, there is no photolysis (splitting) of water. The cyclic flow of electrons results only in the synthesis of ATP, not $\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+$.

Therefore, the correct statement is that it occurs in membrane regions lacking the NADP reductase enzyme.

Answer: It occurs in membrane regions that lack the NADP reductase enzyme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the enzyme RuBisCO:
(I) It is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.
(II) Its binding to $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ is competitive.
(III) It has a much greater affinity for $\mathrm{O}_2$ than for $\mathrm{CO}_2$.
(IV) It catalyzes the conversion of RuBP to oxaloacetic acid (OAA).

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct as RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.

Statement (II) is correct because the active site of RuBisCO can bind to both $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$, and their binding is competitive.

Statement (III) is incorrect because RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for $\mathrm{CO}_2$ than for $\mathrm{O}_2$. It is the relative concentration of these gases that determines which will bind to the enzyme.

Statement (IV) is incorrect because RuBisCO catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP to form two molecules of 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA). Oxaloacetic acid (OAA) is the primary product formed by the activity of PEP carboxylase.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A specific chemical inhibitor completely blocks the functioning of the photosystem whose reaction centre has an absorption maximum at 680 nm. Which of the following physiological processes will be directly and immediately halted as a result?
options: Splitting of water and oxygen evolution
questions.solution:
The photosystem with an absorption maximum at 680 nm is Photosystem II (PS II).

PS II is physically associated with the water-splitting complex located on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane. This complex is responsible for the photolysis of water, which releases electrons, protons, and oxygen.

Therefore, blocking PS II directly halts the splitting of water and the subsequent evolution of oxygen.

Cyclic photophosphorylation and ATP synthesis in stroma lamellae are mediated solely by Photosystem I (PS I), which has an absorption peak at 700 nm. Thus, PS I can continue to absorb light beyond 680 nm and function independently of PS II.

Answer: Splitting of water and oxygen evolution

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Pigments that appear yellow and yellow-orange on a paper chromatogram are crucial for protecting chlorophyll $a$ from photo-oxidation.
Reason (R): These pigments absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll $a$, acting as accessory pigments.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Pigments that appear yellow (xanthophylls) and yellow to yellow-orange (carotenoids) on a paper chromatogram are accessory pigments. One of their crucial functions is to protect chlorophyll $a$ from photo-oxidation.

Reason (R) is correct: These pigments also absorb light of different wavelengths and transfer the energy to chlorophyll $a$, which broadens the spectrum of light used for photosynthesis.

However, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). The fact that they transfer energy to chlorophyll $a$ is a separate parallel function and does not explain the mechanism by which they protect chlorophyll $a$ from photo-oxidation. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the chemiosmotic synthesis of ATP in chloroplasts, a proton gradient is developed across the thylakoid membrane. Which of the following events is directly responsible for the decrease in proton concentration in the stroma?
options: Enzymatic reduction of NADP$^{+}$ by NADP reductase on the stroma side
Splitting of water molecules on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane
Transfer of electrons from Photosystem II to the primary electron acceptor
Flow of protons through the transmembrane channel of ATP synthase
questions.solution:
The proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane is created by the accumulation of protons in the lumen and a decrease in proton concentration in the stroma.

The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the stroma side of the membrane. It requires both electrons (from PS I) and protons to reduce NADP$^{+}$ to NADPH + H$^{+}$. These protons are removed directly from the stroma, causing a decrease in the stromal proton concentration.

Splitting of water adds protons to the lumen, not the stroma. Flow of protons through ATP synthase brings protons back into the stroma, which would increase their concentration there. Transfer of electrons to the primary acceptor does not directly consume protons.

Answer: Enzymatic reduction of NADP$^{+}$ by NADP reductase on the stroma side

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) RuBisCO(I) Chemiosmosis
(B) PEP carboxylase(II) Primary CO_2$ fixation in C_4$ plants
(C) ATP synthase(III) Reduction of NADP$^+$
(D) NADP reductase(IV) Primary CO_2$ fixation in C_3$ plants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
RuBisCO is the primary carboxylating enzyme in C_3$ plants, catalyzing the reaction of RuBP with CO_2$.

PEP carboxylase is the primary carboxylating enzyme in the mesophyll cells of C_4$ plants, fixing CO_2$ to PEP.

ATP synthase is the enzyme complex that facilitates the synthesis of ATP driven by a proton gradient during chemiosmosis.

NADP reductase is an enzyme located on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane, responsible for the reduction of NADP$^+$ to NADPH during the light reaction.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the requirements of chemiosmosis in chloroplasts:

List-IList-II
(A) Membrane(I) Contains a channel for facilitated diffusion of protons
(B) Proton pump(II) Its breakdown provides energy to drive ATP synthesis
(C) Proton gradient(III) Required to create an enclosed space for accumulation of protons
(D) ATP synthase(IV) Transports protons from the stroma into the lumen

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the chemiosmotic hypothesis, ATP synthesis requires a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient, and ATP synthase.

The membrane creates an enclosed space (the thylakoid lumen) to allow the accumulation of protons.

The proton pump actively transports protons from the stroma into the lumen against their concentration gradient.

The proton gradient is the store of energy; its breakdown provides the energy required to drive ATP synthesis.

ATP synthase consists of a $CF_0$ part that acts as a transmembrane channel for the facilitated diffusion of protons across the membrane, and a $CF_1$ part that synthesises ATP.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
