questions.solution: CAM plants do not exhibit the structural compartmentation as shown by $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants which exhibit kranz anatomy. CAM plants fix $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at night because their stomata are open at night and remain closed during the day.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The first carbon dioxide fixation product of $C_4$ plants is
questions.solution: In $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants, initial fixation of carbon dioxide occurs in mesophyll cells. The primary acceptor of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ i.e., phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) combines with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in the presence of PEP carboxylase or PEPcase to form oxaloacetic acid, which is the first stable carbon dioxide fixation product in $\mathrm{C}_4$ pathway.

Light reactions of photosynthesis take place in the presence of light. These involve photolysis of water and production of assimilatory power (NADPH + ATP) through PS I and PS II.
Dark reactions of photosynthesis catalyse assimilation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ to carbohydrates. Dark reactions are light independent reactions, hence can take place both in the light as well as in the dark.

questions.solution: The efficiency of $C_4$ plants is more than those of $C_3$ plants because (i) $C_4$ plants are more efficient in picking up $\mathrm{CO}_2$ even when it is found in low concentration because of the high affinity of PEP, (ii) concentric arrangement of mesophyll cells produces a smaller area in relation to volume for better utilization of available water and reduce the intensity of solar radiations, (iii) they can tolerate excess salts because of the presence of organic acids, (iv) normal oxygen concentration is not inhibitory for the growth in contrast to $C_3$ plants, (v) they are adapted to high temperature and intense radiation of tropics.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Photorespiration shows formation of
questions.solution:
Photorespiration is the light dependent process of oxygenation of ribulose biphosphate (RuBP) and release of carbon dioxide by the photosynthetic organs of a plant. Normally photosynthetic organs do the reverse in the light, i.e., uptake of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and release of $\mathrm{O}_2$. At high temperature, RuBP carboxylase functions as oxygenase and instead of fixing carbon dioxide ( $\mathrm{C}_3$ cycle), oxidises ribulose 1,5 -biphosphate to produce a 3-carbon phosphoglyceric acid and a 2-carbon phosphoglycolate.
Photorespiration does not produce energy or reducing power. Rather, it consumes energy. Further, it undoes the work of photosynthesis. There is $25 \%$ loss of fixed $\mathrm{CO}_2$. Therefore, photorespiration is a highly wasteful process. This happens only in case of $C_3$ plants. $C_4$ plants have overcome the problem of photorespiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Kranz anatomy is usually associated with
questions.solution: The $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants are adapted to dry tropical regions and have greater productivity of biomass. They have special type of leaf anatomy known as Kranz anatomy. In this type of anatomy the bundle sheath cells form several layers around the vascular bundles; they are characterized by having a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants are more efficient than $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants.
$\mathrm{C}_3$ plants are more efficient than $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants.
Photorespiration is absent in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants but present in $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants.
questions.solution: $C_4$ plants are more efficient than $C_3$ plants because they have little photorespiration while in $C_3$ plants more than half of photosynthetic carbon get lost in photorespiration. $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants are more efficient in picking up $\mathrm{CO}_2$, even in low $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration because of high affinity of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ with PEP (phosphoenol pyruvic acid).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: The first step in photosynthesis is the light-driven oxidation (splitting or photolysis) of water. It provides the electrons for the photosynthetic electron transport chains as well as protons for the establishment of a proton gradient. It occurs on the lumenal side of the thylakoid membrane. During photolysis, water is oxidised to oxygen, protons and electrons. Protons accumulate in the lumen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves
questions.solution: Cyclic photophosphorylation is a process of photophosphorylation in which an electron expelled by the excited photocentre is returned to it after passing through a series of electron carriers. Cyclic photophosphorylation is performed by photosystem I only. The electron is circulated within the photosystem and the phosphorylation occurs due to cyclic flow of electron. The excited electron does not pass on to $\mathrm{NADP}^{+}$but is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain. The cyclic flow hence, results only in the synthesis of ATP, but not of $\mathrm{NADPH}+\mathrm{H}^{+}$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The first stable product of Calvin cycle is
questions.solution:
Calvin pathway occurs in all photosynthetic plants which is $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation cycle. Carbon dioxide combines with ribulose-1, 5-biphosphate (RuBp) to produce a transient intermediate compound.
The intermediate compound splits up immediately in the presence of water to form the two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate or 3-PGA. It is the first stable product of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Due to pollution atmospheric concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is increasing which will be harmful for $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants whereas productivity is going to increase for $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants.
Reason : $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants have greater efficiency for $\mathrm{CO}_2$ as $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is fixed by PEP oxygenase.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration of the atmosphere is $0.036 \%$ or $360 \mathrm{ppm}\left(360 \mu l . l^{-1}\right)$. It is a limiting factor for $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants as the available $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration is lower than the optimum for photosynthesis. Increase in its concentration upto $0.05 \%$ increases the rate of photosynthesis in most $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants. When $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration is reduced, there comes a point at which illuminated plant parts stop absorbing carbon dioxide from their environment. It is known as $\mathrm{CO}_2$ compensation point or threshold value. At this value $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixed in photosynthesis is equal to $\mathrm{CO}_2$ evolved in respiration and photorespiration. The value is $25-100 \mathrm{ppm}$ in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants and $0-10 \mathrm{ppm}$ in $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants. The reason for low compensation value for $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants is the greater efficiency of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation through PEP-carboxylase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the characteristic of PS-I?
options: It is active only upto $680 \mathrm{~nm}$ of light.
The reaction centre of PS-I is $\mathrm{P}_{680}$.
PS-I is reduced by the electrons released in photolysis of water.
PS-I is involved in non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
questions.solution: Photosystem I is located in the nonappressed part of grana thylakoids as well as stroma thylakoids. In this photosystem chlorophyll : carotenoid content is high. Its photocentre is $\mathrm{P}_{700}$. Pigment molecules of PS I absorb at or below 700 $\mathrm{nm}$ wavelenth of light. It receives electrons from photosystem II. Photosystem I is involved in both cyclic and non cyclic photophosphorylation. It is not connected with photolysis of water. Usually it hands over its electron to $\mathrm{NADP}^{+}$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Dark reaction occurs only at night in the stroma of chloroplast.
Reason : $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation occurs only during $\mathrm{C}_3$ cycle.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Dark reaction is also known as lightindependent phase. Unlike, light reaction, it does not require light as an essential factor. Thus can takes place both in the presence or absence of light. The term dark reaction does not mean that it takes place only in dark period or at night. $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation occurs in both $\mathrm{C}_3$ and $\mathrm{C}_4$ cycle. In $\mathrm{C}_3$ cycle, $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is added by the enzyme, RuBisco to a 5 carbon compound RuBP that is converted to 2 molecules of 3-carbon PGA. In $\mathrm{C}_4$ cycle the first product of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation (takes place in mesophyll) is a 4-carbon compound, oxaloacetic acid. It is seen in some tropical plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The higher concentration of \(\mathrm{O}_2\) in the atmosphere is inhibitory to photosynthesis.
Reason : \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) is the main substrate of photosynthesis.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Oxygen accumulation causes substantial inhibition of photosynthesis. Both oxygen evolution and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ assimilation were reduced in the presence of atmospheric oxygen. Oxygen causes a direct and indeed competitive inhibition of Ribulose diphosphate carboxylase. As a result glycolate synthesis is enhanced and leads to begin photorespiration. Carbon dioxide being one of the raw materials for photosynthesis, its concentration affects the rate of photosynthesis markedly. Because of its very low concentration in atmosphere $(0.03$ per cent only) it acts as a limiting factor in natural photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is PAR range?
questions.solution: Light is the visible part of electromagnetic radiations. Sunlight or solar radiations reaching the earth have wavelength between \(300 \mathrm{~nm}\) to \(2600 \mathrm{~nm}\). Part of the spectrum used in photosynthesis has a wavelength between \(400-700 \mathrm{~nm}\). It is called photosynthetically active radiation (PAR).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Dark reaction is purely enzymatic reaction.
Reason : It occurs only in absence of light.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Photosynthesis is actually oxidation reduction process in which water is oxidised and \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) is reduced to carbohydrates. Assimilatory power ATP and \(\mathrm{NADPH}_2\) are required for reduction of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\). But this reduction is independent of light i.e occurs in presence or absence of light but production of assimilatory power is light dependent. This reaction is called light reaction or Hill's reaction and the light independent phase is an enzymatic reaction called dark reaction. It occurs is stroma of chloroplast and is enzyme radiated one. It was first of all established by F.F. Blackman and so is also called Blackman's reaction. During this process \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) is fixed to carbohydrate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Under conditions of high light intensity and limited $\mathrm{CO}_2$ supply, photorespiration has a useful role in protecting the plants from photo-oxidative damage.
Reason : If enough $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is not available to utilize light energy for carboxylation to proceed, the excess energy may not cause damage to plants.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
questions.solution: Photorespiration protects the plants from photoxidative damage by dissipating excess of excitation energy. When the $\mathrm{CO}_2$ supply is limited and under high light intensity photorespiration takes place thus protecting the plants. If enough $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is not available to utilize light energy for carboxylation to proced, the excess energy will cause photoxidative damage to the plants. The energy liberated should be used in photophosphorylation in presence of $\mathrm{CO}_2$. If $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is less then in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants $\mathrm{O}_2$ combines with $\mathrm{RuBP}$ to form phosphoglycollate thus utilizing the excess energy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Photosynthetically $C_4$ plants are less efficient than $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants.
Reason : The operation of $\mathrm{C}_4$ pathway requires the involvement of only bundle-sheath cells.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
questions.solution: $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants are those plants that produce $\mathrm{C}_4$ compound like malic acid or aspartic acid as the first stable compound of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation cycle, eg. maize, sugar cane etc. These plants can grow in dense tropical, forests where there is poor supply of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ because there is internal supply of $\mathrm{CO}_2$. Also photorespiration is negligible or absent in these plants. So, they are photosynthetically more efficient than $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants. These plants show a special type of leaf anatomy called Kranz anatomy. $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants uses mesophyll cells and bundle sheath cells in the outer part of their leaves. The $\mathrm{C}_4$ pathway shows 2 carboxylation reactions one in mesophyll chloroplast and the other in bundle sheath. Chloroplasts $-\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor is PEP and not RuBP and PEP carboxylase is the key enzyme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : $C_4$ photosynthetic pathway is more efficient than the $\mathrm{C}_3$ pathway.
Reason : Photorespiration is suppressed in $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C}_4$ photosynthetic pathway is more efficient than $\mathrm{C}_3$ pathway as $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants can pick up $\mathrm{CO}_2$ even when it is found in low concentration. PEP enzymes shows high affinity for $\mathrm{CO}_2 . \mathrm{C}_4$ plants contain two types of chloroplast (Kranz anatomy) : bundle sheath chloroplast and mesophyll chloroplast. Bundle sheath cells contain Calvin cycle enzymes. Due to high concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in bundle sheath cells, RuBP carboxylase works only for Calvin cycle and not for photorespiration.
Photorespiration is a wasteful process as it works to undo the act of photosynthesis in $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants. No energy rich compound is produced in this process. When temperature increase more and more photosynthetically fixed carbon is lost by photorespiration thus reducing the efficiency of $C_3$ plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The atmospheric concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at which photosynthesis just compensates for respiration is referred to as $\mathrm{CO}_2$ compensation point
Reason: The $\mathrm{CO}_2$ compensation point is reached when the amount of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ uptake is less than that generated through respiration because the level of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in the atmosphere is more than that required for achi eving $\mathrm{CO}_2$ compensation point.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion

questions.solution: At very low $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration photosynthesis is strongly limited by the 1 ow $\mathrm{CO}_2$ while respiratory rates are unaffected. As a result there is a negative balance between $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixed by photosynthesis and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ produced by respiration and a net efflux of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ from the plant. By increasing the atmospheric concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at which photosynthesis just compensate for respiration is referred to as $\mathrm{CO}_2$ compensation point.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following categories of organisms do not evolve oxygen during photosynthesis?
questions.solution: The photosynthetic bacteria (e.g. purple non-sulphur bacteria) photosynthesise using bacteriochlorophylls $a$ and $b$ in anoxic environments, such as the bottom mud of ponds and other stagnant water, although they are able to survive in air. The reducing agent involved is hydrogen rather than water, so oxygen is not produced. These bacteria efficiently use infrared light for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The photorespiratory carbon-oxidation cycle involves the interaction of
questions.solution: Photorespiration is a metabolic pathway that occurs in plants in the presence of light, in which ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase the (RuBisCO) enzyme involved in carbon dioxide fixation with ribulose bisphosphate, accepts oxygen, in place of carbon dioxide, resulting in the formation of a twocarbon compound, glycolate. Most of the fixed carbon represented by the glycolate can be salvaged by a series of reactions-the glycolate pathway - involving the peroxisomes and mitochondria, and returned to the chloroplasts. However, some of the carbon is lost as carbon dioxide. Unlike respiration there is no production of ATP.

questions.solution: The opening and closing of stomata is a function of turgor changes in guard cells. In light malic acid is produced in guard cells which dissociates into hydrogen and malate ions, resulting in intake of $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions through $\mathrm{H}^{+}-\mathrm{K}^{+}$ion exchange. There is increase in concentration of $\mathrm{K}^{+}$and malate ions in guard cells, endosmosis of water into guard cells occurs resulting in increased turgor pressure which results in stomatal opening. Stomata are chiefly concerned with gaseous exchange during photosynthesis and respiration and water loss through transpiration.

to the presence of two types of chloroplasts agranal in bundle sheath cells and grand in mesophyll cells ,e.g. sugarcane, maize, etc. In these plants, the first stable product after the fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is 4-c, dicarboxylic acid called Oxaloacetic Acid (OAA).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chl -b differs from chl -a by
questions.solution: Chlorophyll-b structrally differs from chlorophyll-a by the presence of carbonyl (CHO) group at 3rd carbon in the prophyrin ring. chlorophyll-a possess methyl $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)$ group in this place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Molecular formula of chlorophyll-b is
questions.solution: The molecular formula of chlorophyll-b is $\mathrm{C}_{55} \mathrm{H}_{70} \mathrm{O}_6 \mathrm{~N}_4 \mathrm{Mg}$. It helps in photosynthesis by absorbing light energy. It is more soluble in polar solvents than chlorophyll-a because of its carbonyl group. It is of yellow colour and primarily absorbs blue light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these is incorrect for $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants?
questions.solution: Among the given options, option (4) is incorrect about $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants. The mesophyll cells of $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants do not possess RuBisCO enzyme. $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants show Kranz anatomy. In these plants, the initial fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ occurs in mesophyll cells. The primary acceptor of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is Phosphoenol Pyruvate or PEP. It combines with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in the presence of PEP carboxylase or PEPCase to form oxaloacetic acid or oxaloacetate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Conditions required for cyclic photophosphorylation are
questions.solution:
The conditions required for cyclic photophosphorylation are aerobic condition and optimum light intensity.
It is a process of photophosphorylation in which an electron expelled by the excited photocentre is returned. This electron passes through a series of electron carriers. Cyclic photophosphorylation is performed by photosystem-I only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Herbicide that blocks electron transport from PS-II to PS-I by inhibiting electron flow between plastoquinone → cytochrome is
questions.solution:
DCMU is selective herbicide that acts as a potent inhibitor of PS-II. Paraquat inhibits PS-I by producing super oxides.
DCPIP is a dye used to measure rate of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A plant is provided with ideal conditions for photosynthesis and supplied with isotope 14 $\mathrm{CO}_2$. When the products of the process are analysed carefully, what would be the nature of products?
options: Oxygen is labelled, but glucose is normal
Glucose is labelled, but oxygen is normal
questions.solution:
In the process of photosynthesis
$6 \mathrm{CO}_2+12 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{Chl}]{\mathrm{hv}}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_6+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+6 \mathrm{O}_2 \uparrow \\ & \text { (Glucose) }\end{aligned}$
Plants manufacture glucose from $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and oxygen gas is released. So, due to isotopic carbon of $\mathrm{CO}_2$, only glucose will be labelled, but oxygen will be normal.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Fixation of one $\mathrm{CO}_2$ molecule through Calvin cycle requires.
questions.solution: 2 ATP are required during conversion of PGA to 1, 3 diphosphoglyceric acid and 1 ATP during conversioin of glyceraldehyde phosphate to ribulose biphosphate. $2 \mathrm{NADPH}_2$ molecules are utilised for converting 1, 3 diphosphoglyceric acid to glyceraldehyde phosphate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following elements is activator for both ribulose bisphosphate, carboxylase oxygenase and phosphoenol pyruvate carboxylase in photosynthetic carbon fixation?
questions.solution: In photosynthetic carbon fixation magnesium ion $\left(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\right)$ is an activator for both ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase oxygenase and phosphoenol pyruvate carboxylase enzymes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following characteristics out of I, II and III are exhibited by $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants?
I. Kranz anatomy.
II. The product of photosynthesis is oxalo acetic acid.
III. Both PEP carboxylase and ribulose-bis phosphate carboxylase act as carboxylating enzyme.
Choose the corrent option.
options: I and II, but not III
II and III, but not I
I and III, but not II
questions.solution: $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants have an alternative $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation pathways called Hatch and Slack cycle where OAA, a 4C compound is the first stable product. These plants have Kranz anatomy in leaf.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In photosynthesis carbon dioxide is converted to carbohydrates. It is a _______ process.
questions.solution: Photosynthesis is an oxidation reduction process in which water is oxidised and carbon dioxide is reduced to carbohydrates. Hence, it is anabolic and endergonic process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following characteristics is are exhibited by $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants?
I. Kranz anatomy.
II. The first product of photosynthesis is oxaloacetic acid.
III. Both PEP carboxylates and ribulose biphosphate carboxylate act as carboxylating enzymes.
The correct option is
options: I and III, but not II
I and II, but not III
II and III, but not I
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C}_4$-plants have an alternative $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation pathway called Hatch and Slack cycle. These plants have Kranz anatomy in leaf, where vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath.
In $\mathrm{C}_4$ cycle light reaction occurs in, mesophyll chloroplast by PEP carboxylaes and the assimilation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ takes place in, i.e., dark phase in bundle sheath chloroplast by Rubisco.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Quantasome are present in
questions.solution: Quantasomes are the photosynthetic units present in the thylakoids of chloroplast. Each of the quantasomes contain about 250-300 chlorophyll molecules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following cell organelles is associated with photorespiration?
questions.solution: Photorespiration ( $\mathrm{C}_2$-cycle) is a special type of respiration shown by many green plants ( $\mathrm{C}_3$-plants) when they are exposed to light. It is a light dependent process during, which $\mathrm{O}_2$ is used and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is released. The process of photorespiration takes place only in chlorophyllous tissues of plants. Therefore, the main site for photorespiration is chloroplast. But mitochondria and peroxysomes are also required to complete the process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Kranz anatomy can be obseved in leaves of
questions.solution: Kranz anatomy is found in $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants, e.g., Sorghum, Zea mays, Saccharum officinarum. It is characterised by connective, undifferentiated mesophyll around vascular bundles with chloroplast containing bundle sheath.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Light reaction in stroma lamellae of the chloroplast results in the formation of
questions.solution: Photosystem-I is located in non-appressed part of grana and stroma lamellae. It is involved both in cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation. Interrelationship of PS-I and PS-II produces ATP and $\mathrm{NADPH}_2$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In leaves of $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants malic acid synthesis during $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation occurs in
questions.solution: In $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants $\mathrm{CO}_2$ combines with phosphoenol pyruvic acid to form oxaloacetic acid in mesophyll chloroplasts. It is further reduced to malic acid which is transferred to chloroplast in bundle sheath cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In sea anemone, the symmetry is
questions.solution:
In radial symmetry, body can be divided into similar halves by more than two planes passing through the main axis.
Cnidarians or coelenterates (like Hydra, sea anemone, Aurelia, Obelia) are radially symmetrical animals with cell-tissue grade of body organization.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Aqueous and vitreous humour are divided by
questions.solution: Lens is a transparent, biconvex, elastic structure that bends light waves as they pass through its surfaces. The lens separates the aqueous and vitreous humours.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In CAM plants, $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor is
questions.solution: The process of photosynthesis in $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants and CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) is same. But instead of spatial separation of initial PEP case fixation and final Rubisco fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$, the two steps occur in same cell but at different times, night and day, eg, Opuntia, pineapple, Vanilla. PEP (Phosphoenol Pyruvate) is the first acceptor of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in CAM plants like $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Photosynthesis in $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants is relatively less limited by atmospheric $\mathrm{CO}_2$ levels because
options: four carbon acids are the primary initial $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation products
the primary fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is mediated via PEP carboxylase
effective pumping of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ into bundle sheath cells
RUBISCO in $\mathrm{CO}_4$ plants has higher affinity for $\mathrm{CO}_2$
questions.solution:
The fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants takes place in two places and by two different organic compounds. Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) is found in mesophyll cells which primarily fixes atmospheric $\mathrm{CO}_2$ into oxaloacetic acid (4C).
RUBISCO is present in bundle sheath cells where final fixation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in hexose sugars takes place. $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is primarily fixed by PEP carboxylase because this enzyme has greater affinity to $\mathrm{CO}_2$ than RUBISCO.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chemiosmotic theory of ATP synthesis in the chloroplasts and mitochondria is based on
questions.solution: Chemiosmotic hypothesis for oxidative phosphorylation (ATP synthesis) was proposed by Peter Mitchell in 1961 for this he was awarded Noble Prize in 1978. This theory is based on proton gradient.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Photosynthetic Active Radiation (PAR) has the following range of wavelengths
questions.solution: The cosmic rays, X-rays, UV-rays, the visible spectrum, infra red rays, radio waves, coming from sun are constituted electromagnetic spectrum. The waves of each of these types have a characteristic range of wavelengths. The visible spectrum, which is also known as Photosynthetic Active Radiation (PAR), has a range of wavelength of 380 nm to 760 nm . This part of electromagnetic spectrum is responsible for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The law of limiting factors for photosynthesis was enunciated by :
questions.solution: Blackman (1905) proposed the law of limiting factor according to which, "when a biological process is controlled as to its rapidity by a number of separate factors, the rate of the process is limited by the pace of the slowest factor.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant Cuscuta shows maximum photosynthesis in :
questions.solution: Cuscuta is a parasitic plant which gets prepared food from other plants through the haustoria. At this plant lacks chlorophyll, it is unable to perform photosynthesis or to make its own food itself.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The light phase of photosynthesis is called :
questions.solution: Hill reaction, also called as light reaction is a photochemical reaction. In this, reduced enzymes and phosphate bond energy (ATP) are produced.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In photosythesis action and absorption spectrum were related by
questions.solution: Engelmann studied the effect of different region of the visible spectrum on the rate of photosynthesis of different algae. The amount of oxygen $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$ released was found to be maximum in blue and red absorption bands of chlorophyll.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Energy transfer in photosynthesis occurs as
questions.solution: Photosynthetic pigments mainly occur on thylakoid membranes. These are major pigments like chlorophylls and accessory pigments like phycoerythrin, phycocyanin, and carotenoids. The accessory pigments absorb light energy of various wavelength and get excited and transfer the energy to chlorophyll-a molecule through electron spin resonance. Order of energy transfer in photosynthesis occur as phycocyanin followed by phycoerythrin followed by carotenoids and finally to chlorophylls.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In photosynthesis what occurs in PS-II?
options: It takes longer wavelength of light and $e^{-}$ from $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
It takes shorter wavelength of light and $e^{-}$from $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
It takes longer wavelength of light and $e^{-}$ from NADP
It takes shorter wavelength of light and $e^{-}$from NADP
questions.solution: Green plants and algae use two type of photo-system called PS-I and PS -II. In PS-I chlorophyll absorb maximum at 700 nm wavelength of light thus reaction centre is $\mathrm{P}_{700}$ and PS-II absorb maximum 680 nm wavelength of light thus reaction centre is $\mathrm{P}_{680} . \mathrm{P}_{680}$ (PS-II) extracts an electron from water, returning to its unexcited state because hydrolysis of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ occurs in PS-II. So, $\mathrm{O}_2$ evolved in PS-II come from water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Hatch and Slack pathway
options: occurs in Kranz anatomy where mesophyll have small chloroplast whereas bundle sheath have granal chloroplast
occurs in Kranz anatomy when mesophyll have small chloroplast where as bundle sheath have larger, agranal chloroplast
Kranz anatomy where mesophyll cell are diffused
questions.solution: $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants have "Kranz type" anatomy. Vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath cells. The chloroplasts are dimorphic. The cells of bundle sheath have very large chloroplasts. They lack grana and contain starch grains. They are centripetally arranged and mesophyll cells have small and agranal chloroplast.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Hatch and Slack type plants $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor is
questions.solution: In Hatch and Slack cycle $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor is phosphoenol pyruvic acid and first product is oxaloacetic acid, (a $4-\mathrm{C}$ compound). Therefore it is popularly termed as $\mathrm{C}_4$ cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In CAM plants
options: stomata open in day and close at night
stomata remain open in day and night both
stomata remain closed in day and night both
stomata open at night and close in day
questions.solution: CAM is found in members of the family Crassulaceae (e.g., Kalanchoe), family Cactaceae (e.g., Opuntia, Cereus), and some members of Liliaceae, Orchidaceae, Bromeliaceae, Euphorbia sp. All CAM plants are not succulent and stomata open at night.
